claims.text: Real-time machine-learning control can adaptively modulate laser power during L-PBF of AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Adaptive laser-power modulation can reduce residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load L-PBF.
Adaptive laser-power modulation can improve the microstructural and mechanical properties of L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder with a particle size suitable for miniature fabrication is the applicable initial feedstock.
Melt-pool temperature and geometry measurements can provide feedback for real-time adjustment of laser power or pulse parameters.
The applicable geometry consists of miniature components with overall dimensions below 15 mm.
AlCrFeNiSi should be processed in a low-to-moderate energy-input window rather than at constant high power.
Pulse-modulated laser settings are suitable for implementing the proposed low-to-moderate energy-input window.
Reduced thermal gradients produce smoother and more uniform melt-pool solidification.
Smoother and more uniform solidification produces a refined, homogeneous microstructure with fewer stress concentrations.
Adaptive pulse-energy control lowers peak local temperatures and thermal gradients.
Lower peak temperatures and thermal gradients minimize rapid cooling and abrupt solidification.
Minimizing rapid cooling and abrupt solidification reduces residual stress and preserves microstructural integrity.
Adaptive processing will yield finer and more uniform microstructures than conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Adaptive processing will increase tensile strength and ductility relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Adaptive machine-learning control will simplify overall processing complexity.
Conventional constant high-energy-input L-PBF builds exhibit high residual stresses and microstructural heterogeneities.
The proposed intervention may not apply to larger builds or to regimes dominated by melt-pool instability.
